description: Mechanically checkable subset of voices/whit3rabbit.md. Everything here is a hard rule for this writer. Judgment rules stay in the markdown.
banned_phrases: at the end of the day

banned_regex.label: Condescension by seniority
banned_regex.rx: (?i)(if you'?d been (doing this|here) as long as|when you'?ve been (doing this|around) as long as|with all due respect,)
banned_regex.example: With all due respect, the schedule was never realistic.

banned_regex.label: Fear-mongering
banned_regex.rx: (?i)(before it'?s too late|you can'?t afford (not )?to|the (threat|risk) has never been (greater|higher)|it'?s only a matter of time before you'?re)
banned_regex.example: Patch the gateway before it's too late.

banned_regex.label: Absolute security claim
banned_regex.example: The appliance is 100% secure out of the box.

banned_regex.label: War metaphor on desk work
banned_regex.rx: (?i)\b(battle ?rhythm|kill chain|in the trenches|war ?room|weaponi[sz]e[ds]?|force multiplier|troops on the ground|boots on the ground)
banned_regex.example: The team ran a war room for three days.

banned_regex.label: Overused efficiency/improve
banned_regex.note: Not banned, overused. Two uses pass; the third and every one after it is flagged. Name what got faster or better instead.
banned_regex.example: Efficiency improves when the process improves.

banned_regex.label: Motivational-poster cadence
banned_regex.note: Three consecutive one-sentence paragraphs. Write in sentences.
banned_regex.example:
Ship the work.

Measure the result.

Then do it again.

banned_regex.label: Tidy over-hedging
banned_regex.rx: (?i)\b(i (just )?wanted to (reach out|check in|follow up)|i was (just )?wondering if|if that (makes|would make) sense|does that (sound|work) (good|ok)|no worries (at all|if not))
banned_regex.example: I just wanted to check in on the draft.

banned_regex.label: Manufactured enthusiasm
banned_regex.rx: (?i)(i'?m (so |really |super )?(excited|thrilled|pumped) to|we'?re (thrilled|excited) to announce|can'?t wait to|absolutely love(d)? (this|it)|amazing work!|fantastic job!)
banned_regex.example: We're thrilled to announce the new release.

banned_regex.label: Credential as substitute for substance
banned_regex.example: As a certified network engineer, I would not do that.

required_when.label: Missing closer
required_when.note: Which closer depends on the rung: 'Thanks,' + '-whit3rabbit' at chat, informal, and blog, 'v/r' at formal. Only checked when the text opens like correspondence, which is why it is scoped to the spine and not to the genre columns: a README does not take a signoff.

preferred_substitutions.circle back: follow up, get back to you, revisit
preferred_substitutions.bad actor: attacker, the person who did it
